answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by issuing reputation that fades like a zephyr: credentials expire unless renewed by fresh, verifiable work, so a farm cannot hoard standing forever. The summit of this design is a decay curve where each credential loses weight over time and must be re-earned. Its failure mode is a burst farm that does one big job, then coasts on the glow; the check is a public audit comparing credential age against recent work proofs, revoking any badge whose horizon of activity has gone quiet.
